findings.source_en: From death you were born, from death you shall return.
findings.ar: من الموت وُلدت، وإلى الموت ستعود.
findings.issue: The English says FROM death you shall return - the cultists' creed about the Harbinger's resurrection (this master tree ends with [Respawn Dialogue]). The Arabic flips the preposition to إلى, turning it into the ordinary 'to death you shall return' and destroying the resurrection doctrine the line states.
findings.suggested_ar: من الموت وُلدت، ومن الموت ستعود.

findings.source_en: Now leave us. I will take care of Gorf.
findings.issue: Number agreement: 'us' is the object (Hilga and Gorf); the addressee is the Harbinger, singular. اتركونا is a plural imperative and addresses a group that is not there.

findings.ar: حسنًا، آسفة، يا صاحبي. هيلغا بالخارج.
findings.issue: 'brev' is frozen as يا صاح. Same violation as two rows in chunk 047.
findings.suggested_ar: حسنًا، آسفة، يا صاح. هيلغا بالخارج.

findings.issue: كاملة = 'complete/whole', not 'perfect'. It also collides with 'I am… complete' (أنا… مكتملة) five rows later, blurring two different claims.
